facts.text: The satsuma is a mandarin, Citrus unshiu, first reported in Japan more than 700 years ago (an origin in China is also argued) and named in the West for the old Satsuma province, now Kagoshima Prefecture; it was introduced to the West from the Satsuma region in 1878. It is usually seedless and peels easily.

In Louisiana satsumas are more than three quarters of the citrus acreage, and Plaquemines Parish is the centre of production. They ripen in the fall: some from late September, later ones into late November or early December, and they sell into late December. Colour is not a sure sign of sweetness.

Belgian endive (witloof, the Flemish for white leaf) is chicory grown from roots forced in the dark, which keeps the leaves white, compact and only gently bitter; light turns them green and bitter. It was developed around Brussels in the 1830s (a popular legend says 1830; a gardener of the Brussels Botanical Garden is credited with the method in the winter of 1834 to 1835) and was sold in Brussels markets by 1846 or 1867, the sources differ. Curly endive is a different chicory; both are of the chicory family.
The sunflower, Helianthus annuus, is native to North America, and its domestication is traced to eastern North America (a Mexican origin is also argued).
